description:
## Mandatory context and boundaries
Read the parent epic first. Applicable owners: AGENTS.md; docs/agent-tools.md; docs/WORKFLOW_AGENT.md; docs/exec-plans/PLAN_STRATEGY.md; docs/action-reuse.md; docs/testing-approach.md; docs/services/channels.md (communication/Jido bridge and provider contracts); docs/services/engine.md (history, admission, finalization and delivery). Read docs/documentation.md before documentation/skill edits, docs/services/system-config.md before credential fixtures, and local module @moduledoc before extending a helper. Apply code-quality for code and skill-creator for the skill.
Only test/ additions or backward-compatible support changes, lib/mix/tasks/zaq.test.gen.channel.ex, and .agents/skills/add-channel-integration-tests/** are authorized. Do not edit application modules, dependency source/pins, config, migrations, mix.exs, CI, or unrelated skills. Existing-test expectation changes require the testing handbook's explicit approval; this epic authorizes additive coverage, not changing expectations.
Use real bridges, NodeRouter, Engine admission/history/persistence and configured Agent execution. Only provider/LLM boundaries are faked. A production defect is a reported blocker with a reproducer; do not patch production, silently omit a scenario, weaken an assertion, or close the issue as complete.
Validation timing, failure handling and final gates are owned by docs/WORKFLOW_AGENT.md. Record executed commands/results in this issue. No new browser E2E is needed: this work adds test/developer infrastructure without changing a deployed UI journey. No commit/push/merge authorization is implied.

Parent epic: zaq-o9d

## Functional specification and files
Add test/support/channels/integration/drivers/telegram.ex and test/zaq/channels/integration/providers/telegram_test.exs; register Drivers.Telegram. Reuse the saved URL/local HTTP setup in telegram_history_delivery_test.exs and native webhook envelope fields from jido_chat_bridge/telegram_reaction_webhook_test.exs without copying its CapturingNodeRouter.
start/1 starts a local Bot API fake and returns an endpoint, synthetic bot token, sender/chat ids and actual Jido.Chat.Telegram.Adapter registration. connect/2 starts the real webhook bridge; native requests enter through JidoChatBridge.handle_webhook/2 (and normal configured webhook verification where applicable). Do not call transform_incoming/to_internal directly as the shared-suite entry point.
Build native updates with unique update_id, chat-local message_id, from, date, chat type and mention entities/bot identity. Direct uses private chat; shared uses group/supergroup. Include reply/topic fields only when supported by the inspected adapter.
HTTP fake must understand the actual send/edit/typing/profile/webhook calls used by the suite, including current rich-message versus plain text encoding where applicable. Return faithful ok/result/error responses and preserve chat-local message ids. Use existing local-server helpers rather than a new HTTP stack.
For callbacks not exposed through URL (if encountered), use a test-only delegating adapter wrapper confined to this driver file; do not add production options. First prefer the evidenced URL seam and report precisely any wrapper used.
Capabilities must be evidenced by current adapter APIs. Do not claim single-message root fetching when the adapter declares it unsupported; mention-policy lookup must fail closed appropriately.

## Tests to add before implementation
- Valid direct/shared webhook -> real handler -> provider delivery; malformed/rejected webhook produces no fabricated answer.
- Same message_id in distinct chats/connector configs maps to distinct histories.
- Outgoing send/edit payloads preserve recipient/reply targets and current formatting.
- Successful and failed provider API envelopes; unchanged edit behaviour reuses the existing contract.
- Unexpected requests fail, capabilities match actual support, and scripted terminal failure is not consumed by typing/status.
- Run telegram_history_delivery_test.exs, telegram_markdown_delivery_test.exs and relevant webhook tests without altering expectations.

## Branches/paths validated
Private/group/supergroup native facts, message/update dedupe, successful creation/update, provider errors, room-local ids, supported versus unsupported thread/root operations.

## Mocking plan
Loopback Telegram HTTP service and existing LLM server only. Real Telegram adapter, Jido webhook parsing, NodeRouter, Engine/Agent/history throughout.

## Documentation
Record native webhook entry point, supported Bot API endpoints and capability limitations in driver docs/README. Link the existing test evidence.

## Action reuse assessment
Reuse real Jido.Chat.Telegram.Adapter and current local HTTP support; new fake routes are local-only test code. No application Action or domain implementation is added. Verify exact request payloads and real persisted outcomes, preserving existing delivery contracts.

## Done when
Telegram is registered and passes the common driver contract plus provider-specific scenarios; real adapter HTTP calls target only the fake endpoint, with no production/config/dependency changes.

comments.text:
Implementation is present in the working tree: native Telegram webhook driver, local Bot API HTTP fake using the real adapter/ExGram URL seam, response scripting, registry entry and provider tests. Default-policy direct/shared round trips and HTTP-error handling pass.
Two planned scenarios expose production/dependency defects: zaq-kxd (native mentions dropped by mention_required because was_mentioned remains false) and zaq-imv (same message_id in different chats deduped before scoped capture). Both retain failing executable reproducers in test/zaq/channels/integration/providers/telegram_test.exs; no flags are synthesized in the fake and no test is skipped/weakened.
Final current validation: mix q in the default dev environment passed. mix test test/zaq/channels/integration test/zaq/channels/mattermost_shared_history_integration_test.exs test/zaq/channels/jido_chat_delivery_test.exs test/zaq/channels/telegram_history_delivery_test.exs test/zaq/channels/telegram_markdown_delivery_test.exs completed with 75 tests, 2 properties, 2 failures, solely the new Telegram reproducers. Existing tests passed. The earlier Mattermost-only validation passed all 53 tests + 2 properties.
Scope audit: 18 added files, all under test/; no tracked file changes, production/dependency/config changes, commits or pushes. First three children are complete; this child is open and blocked by the two explicit defect tickets. Later children stay unstarted under the approved dependency sequence. Fixing these production/dependency contracts needs new user authorization; this implementation does not change that scope. No final precommit/approval gate was requested because required implementation/tests remain blocked.
